    static string HoldIds() => string.Join(",", Character.GearHold.SelectMany(kv => Enumerable.Repeat(kv.Key, kv.Value)).OrderBy(x => x, StringComparer.Ordinal));
    static string RolledFor(string id) { var f = new ConfigFile(); return f.Load("user://smoke_drops.cfg") == Error.Ok ? (string)f.GetValue("drops", id, "?") : "?"; }
    void Unmeet(params string[] ids)
    {
        foreach (var id in ids) Character.HintsSeen.Remove(id);
        var keep = HintQueue.Where(q => !ids.Contains(q)).ToList(); HintQueue.Clear(); foreach (var q in keep) HintQueue.Enqueue(q);
        if (ids.Contains(HintShowing))
        {   // the card on screen too, as if it had finished: while it shows, Met() is true whatever the trigger does
            typeof(Hints).GetField("_showing", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).SetValue(H.Hints, null);
            Nodes<PanelContainer>(H.Hints).First(p => p.Name == "HintCard").Visible = false;
        }
    }
    // Over a point: the ship -- or, in stasis, its escape pod
    void FlyOver(Vector2 at)
    {
        var s = Me; if (s == null) return;
        if (s.Alive) { s.Position = at; s.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; return; }
        if (typeof(PlayerShip).GetField("_pod", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).GetValue(s) is EscapePod p) { p.Position = at; p.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; }
    }
    // class changes go through the creator path now (there are no class hotkeys)
    // A refit, ANNOUNCED: PilotChanged applies it here and tells every peer, so a multiplayer
    // scenario can fly one of the nine and have the other side see which hull it is. Offline,
    // SendIdentity returns at once, so the solo callers are unchanged.
    async Task SetClass(ShipClass c) { Character.Class = c; H.PilotChanged(); await Wait(0.1); }
    System.Collections.Generic.List<(Vector2 p, float age)> Smoke(Shot t) =>
        (System.Collections.Generic.List<(Vector2 p, float age)>)typeof(Shot).GetField("_smoke", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).GetValue(t);
    // the three projectile classes are one flyer with a row each now (Shots.All)
    System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Shot> InFlight() => Nodes<Shot>().Where(x => x.IsMissile);
    System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Shot> Shells() => Nodes<Shot>().Where(x => x.Kind == Shots.Shell);
    System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<Shot> Slugs() => Nodes<Shot>().Where(x => x.Kind == Shots.Slug || x.Kind == Shots.Scrap);
    Vector2 Scr(Vector2 w) => GetViewport().GetCanvasTransform() * w;
    async Task Park(Vector2 at, float rot = 0) { var s = Me; s.Position = at; s.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; s.Rotation = rot; await Wait(2.5); s.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; }

    // The base menu builds a tab's contents only while that tab is shown.
    void ShowTab(Node panel, string tab)
    {
        var tb = Nodes<Button>(panel).First(b => b.Name == "Tab_" + tab);
        if (!tb.ButtonPressed) tb.ButtonPressed = true;      // fires Toggled -> the tab is built
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // FLY — not a check: a PILOT. It takes every class out in clear space, flies it, shoots with
    // it, presses everything on its bar with a target selected, and stands it in front of a wave.
    // Nothing here asserts a known answer: it MEASURES, and says so. The checks prove what we
    // thought to ask; this is for what we did not.
    //
    //   FLY   a measurement
    //   ISSUE a measurement that does not match what the class's own sheet promises
    //
    // `tools\smoketest\run.ps1 -Fly`. The three flyable classes of the line go first as a control:
    // an ISSUE against one of them is the instrument, not the class.
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    private int _issues;
    private readonly System.Collections.Generic.List<string> _table = new();
    void Note(string s) => GD.Print("FLY   " + s);
    void Issue(string s) { _issues++; GD.Print("ISSUE " + s); }

    // everything about a ship an ability could plausibly move, in one line
    string Snap(PlayerShip s, string id)
    {
        ref var sl = ref s.Sl(id);
        return $"L{sl.Left:0.00} C{sl.Cool:0.00} O{sl.Own:0.0} N{sl.N} st{s.Statuses.Bits} "
             + $"w{(s.WingTarget?.NetId ?? 0)} k{(s.StrikeTarget?.NetId ?? 0)} d{s.TurretsOut} "
             + $"m{(s.Staggered ? 1 : 0)} hp{s.Hp:0}";
    }

    async Task Fly()
    {
        var spot = Hub.BasePos + new Vector2(2600, 2400);          // clear of the belt, the wreck, the dummies and the lane
        Note($"twelve classes, one at a time, in clear space at {spot}");
        foreach (var cd in Classes.All.Where(c => c.Ready).ToList())
        {
            try { await FlyOne(cd, spot); }
            catch (Exception ex) { Issue($"{cd.Name}: flying it threw {ex.GetType().Name}: {ex.Message}"); GD.Print(ex.StackTrace); }
        }
        GD.Print("FLY   ── the table ─────────────────────────────────────────────");
        GD.Print("FLY   class        top u/s (sheet)   180 deg   main DPS (sheet)   12 s under a wave");
        foreach (var row in _table) GD.Print("FLY   " + row);
        GD.Print($"FLY DONE issues={_issues}");
    }

    async Task FlyOne(ClassDef cd, Vector2 spot)
    {
        await SetClass(cd.Id);
        await Wait(0.3);
        var s = Me;
        if (s == null) { Issue($"{cd.Name}: no ship after the refit"); return; }
        var S = s.Stats;
        GD.Print($"FLY   ── {cd.Name} ({S["hull"]:0} hull) ─────────────────────────────");
        foreach (var r in H.Raiders.ToList()) r.TakeDamage(1e12);
        await Wait(0.3);

        // ── THE HELM: does it reach its own top speed, and how long to come about? ──
        s.Position = spot; s.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; s.Rotation = 0f; await Wait(0.3);
        double top = 0;
        KeyDown(global::Godot.Key.W);
        for (int i = 0; i < 60 * 6; i++) { top = Math.Max(top, s.SpeedAhead); await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame); }
        double want = S["max_speed"];
        Note($"{cd.Name}: top speed {top:0} u/s, its sheet says {want:0}");
        if (top < want * 0.95) Issue($"{cd.Name}: never reaches its own top speed ({top:0} of {want:0} u/s)");

        // 180 degrees, at speed, on the rudder
        float last = s.Rotation; double acc = 0, turnT = -1, c0 = s.Clock;
        KeyDown(global::Godot.Key.A);
        for (int i = 0; i < 60 * 10 && turnT < 0; i++)
        {
            await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
            acc += Math.Abs(Mathf.AngleDifference(last, s.Rotation)); last = s.Rotation;
            if (acc >= Math.PI) turnT = s.Clock - c0;
        }
        KeyUp(global::Godot.Key.A); KeyUp(global::Godot.Key.W);
        if (turnT < 0) Issue($"{cd.Name}: cannot turn 180 degrees in 10 s on full rudder at speed");
        else Note($"{cd.Name}: 180 degrees in {turnT:0.0} s at {s.SpeedAhead:0} u/s");

        // ── THE GUNS: a hull that cannot die, held at half their range, six seconds on the trigger ──
        double dps = 0;
        if (S["main_count"] >= 1)
        {
            s.Position = spot; s.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; s.Rotation = 0f; await Wait(0.4);
            var at = spot + new Vector2(0, -(float)S["main_range"] * 0.5f);
            var mark = H.SpawnRaider(at, Enemies.Gunship); mark.Hp = 1e9;
            AimWorld(at); await Wait(0.6);
            double hp0 = mark.Hp, g0 = s.Clock;
            KeyDown(global::Godot.Key.Space);
            for (int i = 0; i < 60 * 6; i++)
            {
                mark.Position = at; s.Position = spot; s.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; AimWorld(at);
                await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
            }
            KeyUp(global::Godot.Key.Space);
            for (int i = 0; i < 60; i++) { mark.Position = at; await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame); }   // the last shells land
            double secs = s.Clock - g0, dealt = hp0 - mark.Hp;
            dps = secs > 0 ? dealt / secs : 0;
            Note($"{cd.Name}: main guns landed {dealt:0} in {secs:0.0} s = {dps:0.0} DPS at {at.DistanceTo(spot):0} u, its sheet says {S.MainDps:0.0}");
            if (S.MainDps > 0 && dps < S.MainDps * 0.5)
                Issue($"{cd.Name}: its main guns land less than half what its sheet promises ({dps:0.0} of {S.MainDps:0.0} DPS) at half their range");
            mark.TakeDamage(1e12); await Wait(0.2);
        }

        // ── THE BAR: press everything on it, with a target selected and enemies about ──
        s.Position = spot; s.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; s.Rotation = 0f;
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { var r = H.SpawnRaider(spot + Vector2.Right.Rotated(i * 2.1f) * 300f); r.Hp = 6000; }
        await Wait(0.6);
        Key(global::Godot.Key.Tab); await Wait(0.3);
        if (H.Selected == null) Issue($"{cd.Name}: Tab picked nothing with three raiders 300 u out");
        foreach (var ab in Abilities.For(cd.Id).Where(a => !a.Open && a.Id != "guns").ToList())
        {
            string before = Snap(s, ab.Id);
            s.UseAbility(ab.Id, H.Selected?.NetId ?? 0);
            await Wait(0.4);
            string after = Snap(s, ab.Id);
            string why = s.FailNote(ab.Id);
            if (why != null) Note($"{cd.Name}: {ab.Short} refused -- {why}");
            else if (before == after) Issue($"{cd.Name}: {ab.Short} did nothing and gave no reason ({after})");
            else Note($"{cd.Name}: {ab.Short} -> {after}");
        }

        // ── TWELVE SECONDS UNDER A WAVE: three webifiers and a gunship, nothing pressed ──
        foreach (var r in H.Raiders.ToList()) r.TakeDamage(1e12);
        await Wait(0.3);
        s.Position = spot; s.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; s.Rotation = 0f;
        s.Restore(s.MaxHp, true, 0);                                   // full hull, whatever the bar just did to it
        await Wait(0.3);
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) H.SpawnRaider(spot + Vector2.Right.Rotated(i * 2.1f) * 320f);
        H.SpawnRaider(spot + new Vector2(0, 760), Enemies.Gunship);
        double hull0 = s.Hp;
        for (int i = 0; i < 60 * 12; i++) await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        double lost = hull0 - s.Hp;
        Note($"{cd.Name}: 12 s under three webifiers and a gunship -- lost {lost:0} of {s.MaxHp:0} hull, {(s.Alive ? "alive" : "DEAD")}");
        if (lost <= 0) Issue($"{cd.Name}: a whole wave on it for 12 s took nothing off its hull -- nothing could reach it");
        foreach (var r in H.Raiders.ToList()) r.TakeDamage(1e12);
        await Wait(0.3);
        if (!s.Alive) { s.Restore(s.MaxHp, true, 0); await Wait(0.4); }

        _table.Add($"{cd.Name,-12} {top,7:0} ({want:0})      {(turnT < 0 ? "  --  " : $"{turnT,5:0.0}s")}   {dps,7:0.0} ({S.MainDps:0.0})     {lost,5:0} of {s.MaxHp:0}{(s.Alive ? "" : "  DEAD")}");
    }

    // ── A REFIT COSTS A LEVEL AND UNDOES THE LAST POINT ──────────────────────────────────────
    // The file records the ORDER points were spent in now, because `Bought` only ever said how
    // many of each a pilot owned -- so "undo the most recent" had nothing to read and a refit
    // could only ever have taken the dearest. Both paths are proved: a pilot with an order, and a
    // file from before there was one.
    // ── THE RANGE TO THE TARGET, under it and on the HUD line ────────────────────────────────
    // The HUD named what was selected and nothing anywhere said how far off it was, which is the
    // figure that decides whether a weapon reaches at all.
    async Task RangeChecks()
    {
        var far = H.Raiders.FirstOrDefault();
        if (far == null) { Check(false, "range readout: no raider to select"); return; }
        H.SelectTarget(far);
        // TWO frames: the first may resume before the Hub's own _Process has run, and the line
        // would then still be the one written for the previous target.
        await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        // Whatever is selected when the line is WRITTEN, not what this asked for: a tutorial hint
        // and the ship's own acquisition both pick targets, and the check is about the readout.
        var shown = H.Selected ?? far;
        double want = Me.Position.DistanceTo(shown.Position);
        var line = Nodes<Label>().Select(l => l.Text).FirstOrDefault(t => t != null && t.Contains("target: "));
        // Read the figure back rather than matching the string: the raider is under way, so the
        // line was written a frame before this measured it and the two round a unit apart.
        var said = line == null ? null : System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex.Match(line, @"\((\d+) u\)");
        Check(said is { Success: true } && line.Contains(shown.Label) && Math.Abs(double.Parse(said.Groups[1].Value) - want) < 30,
              $"the HUD names the target AND says how far off it is: {shown.Label} at {said?.Groups[1].Value ?? "nothing"} u, measured {want:0} u");
        H.ClearSelection();
    }

    // ── LEVELLING A PART WITH SALVAGE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // 100 salvage for the first level and a quarter more each time, stopping at +200%. A level adds
    // 5% to what the part is FOR and nothing to what it takes in exchange, and it belongs to the
    // part ID, because the hold stores counts by id and no instance id exists anywhere.
    // ── A BOSS KEEPS UP WITH THE PILOT IT IS FIGHTING ───────────────────────────────────────────
    // Its hull and damage have always climbed 10% a level; its WIND-UPS and its REACH never moved,
    // so a pilot whose gear and points lengthen its own reach every level would fight each boss
    // from further out and dodge it more easily than the last. One percent a level, compounding:
    // quicker to wind up, faster in flight, longer-armed. The burn of a beam and how often that
    // burn is judged are left alone, because those are the damage and it has a scale of its own.
    // ── AN INSTALLED BUILD THAT CAN BE REPLACED (scripts/Builds.cs) ──────────────────────────
    // Pure, and deliberately so: everything with a decision in it lives in Builds.cs, which has no
    // Godot in it and is LINKED INTO THE LAUNCHER. That is what puts the launcher's whole decision
    // surface on this rung instead of on a manual check -- the launcher itself is then only a
    // window, an HTTPS fetch and a Process.Start, with no branch worth testing.
    //
    // The hashes below are literals, not Builds' own output: e3b0c4... is the SHA-256 of nothing at
    // all, and it is in version/MANIFEST.sha256 twice already (both .gdignore files).
    const string Sha0 = "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855";
    const string Sha1 = "99eb6ce0c4bae313371e4fdb6de49ec6cddfd6ef75b4386f0f4edc1f1afc4eab";

    static string SampleInfo(string build) =>
        "schema=1\n"
      + $"build={build}\n"
      + "launch=WarshipsGame.exe\n"
      + "notes=NOTES.txt\n"
      + "manifest=BUILD.sha256\n"
      + "part=code|code.zip|" + Sha0 + "|3355443\n"
      + "part=runtime|runtime.zip|" + Sha1 + "|73400320\n"
      + "in=code|Warships.pck\n"
      + "in=code|data_Warships_windows_x86_64/Warships.dll\n"
      + "in=runtime|WarshipsGame.exe\n";

    void BuildChecks()
    {
        // ── THE BUILD STRING IS INVISIBLE TO THE PROTOCOL HASH ───────────────────────────────
        // Net.Fingerprint() folds in every static field of every null-namespace type that is
        // IsLiteral or IsInitOnly with a Plain field type -- and string is Plain. A
        // `public static readonly string Build` would therefore enter the hash two peers are
        // matched on, and two BYTE-IDENTICAL builds packed a minute apart would refuse each other
        // at the handshake. Asserted STRUCTURALLY, the way the trap is laid: the member must be a
        // property, and the static field behind it must be neither literal nor init-only.
        var buildProp = typeof(Game).GetProperty("Build", BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static);
        var buildFields = typeof(Game).GetFields(BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static)
                                      .Where(f => f.FieldType == typeof(string) && (f.IsLiteral || f.IsInitOnly)).ToList();
        Check(buildProp != null && buildProp.PropertyType == typeof(string)
              && typeof(Game).GetField("Build", BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static) == null
              && buildFields.All(f => f.Name != "_build")
              && Game.Build == "dev",
              $"the build a player reads is a property over a mutable static, so it cannot enter the protocol hash two peers are matched on -- and outside a release it says so ({Game.Build}; {buildFields.Count} frozen strings on Game, none of them the build)");

        // THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST. A manifest line is text from a download; if it can name a
        // place, it can name the player's characters. %APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\Warships is
        // outside the install, so the rule is simply that nothing may leave the install at all.
        string[] escapes = { "..", "../x", "a/../../b", "/etc/passwd", "C:\\Windows\\x",
                             "data\\Warships.dll", "", "   ", "./x", "a//b" };
        int refused = 0;
        foreach (string bad in escapes)
            try { Builds.CheckRel(bad); } catch (System.IO.InvalidDataException) { refused++; }
        Check(refused == escapes.Length,
              $"a manifest path that leaves the install is refused ({refused} of {escapes.Length}: .., a rooted path, a drive, a backslash, an empty one)");

        // Nothing is EXPANDED, either: a line naming an environment variable is a folder with a
        // silly name inside the install, not a door out of it.
        string root = BuildScratch("pure");
        string appdata = Builds.Resolve(root, "%APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/Warships/characters/x.cfg");
        Check(appdata.StartsWith(System.IO.Path.GetFullPath(root), StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
              && Builds.Resolve(root, "data_Warships_windows_x86_64/Warships.dll")
                       .EndsWith("Warships.dll", StringComparison.Ordinal),
              "a manifest path is never expanded and always lands inside the install");

        // sha256sum's format, strictly -- so `sha256sum -c BUILD.sha256` checks an install by hand.
        var man = Builds.ReadManifest(Sha0 + "  Warships.pck\r\n" + Sha1 + "  data_x/Warships.dll\n");
        Check(man.Count == 2 && man[0].Path == "Warships.pck" && man[0].Sha == Sha0
              && man[1].Path == "data_x/Warships.dll" && man[1].Sha == Sha1,
              $"a release manifest reads as sha256sum writes it, CRLF and all ({man.Count} entries)");
        int badLines = 0;
        foreach (string junk in new[] { "\uFEFF" + Sha0 + "  a.txt", "deadbeef  a.txt", Sha0 + " a.txt" })
            try { var m = Builds.ReadManifest(junk); if (m.Count == 0 || m[0].Path != "a.txt") badLines++; }
            catch (System.IO.InvalidDataException) { badLines++; }
        Check(badLines == 2, $"a BOM is stripped but a short hash and a single space are refused ({badLines} of 3 lines rejected)");

        // BUILD.txt, and the part table it carries.
        BuildInfo info = Builds.ReadInfo(SampleInfo("2026-09-23.ec0d138"));
        BuildPart code = info.PartOf("Warships.pck");
        Check(info.Schema == 1 && info.Build == "2026-09-23.ec0d138" && info.Launch == "WarshipsGame.exe"
              && info.Notes == "NOTES.txt" && info.Manifest == "BUILD.sha256" && info.Parts.Count == 2
              && code != null && code.Id == "code" && code.Asset == "code.zip" && code.Bytes == 3355443
              && code.Sha == Sha0 && code.Paths.Count == 2,
              $"a release says what it is, and its parts are rows ({info.Parts.Count} parts, {code?.Paths.Count} files in {code?.Id})");
        Check(Builds.ReadInfo("schema=1\nbuild=x\nunknown_key=whatever\n").Schema == 1,
              "a key a frozen launcher has never heard of is ignored, not refused");

        // A release that contradicts itself is refused BEFORE anything is downloaded.
        // All three at Sha0 -- the hash of nothing -- so PlantInstall can write empty files and the
        // walk below has a real, checkable match to find.
        var want = Builds.ReadManifest(Sha0 + "  Warships.pck\n" + Sha0 + "  WarshipsGame.exe\n"
                                     + Sha0 + "  data_Warships_windows_x86_64/Warships.dll\n");
        Check(Builds.Validate(info, want) == null, "a release that holds together validates");
        var orphan = Builds.ReadManifest(Sha0 + "  Warships.pck\n" + Sha0 + "  WarshipsGame.exe\n"
                                       + Sha0 + "  sfx/boss.ogg\n");
        Check(Builds.Validate(info, orphan) != null && Builds.Validate(info, orphan).Contains("sfx/boss.ogg"),
              "a file no part holds makes the release malformed, and it says which file");
        Check(Builds.Validate(Builds.ReadInfo("schema=1\nbuild=x\n"), want) != null,
              "a release with no parts and nothing to launch is malformed");

        // THE DECISION TABLE. Every outcome, one literal scenario each.
        string say;
        BuildInfo local = Builds.ReadInfo(SampleInfo("2026-09-20.aaaaaaa"));
        Check(Builds.Decide(root, local, null, null, null, out say) == BuildOutcome.Offline
              && say.Contains("offline"),
              $"no network plays what is installed rather than refusing ({say})");
        Check(Builds.Decide(root, local, Builds.ReadInfo("schema=99\nbuild=z\n"), null, null, out say) == BuildOutcome.LauncherTooOld,
              $"a release from the future asks for a newer launcher instead of breaking ({say})");
        Check(Builds.Decide(root, local, info, null, "no part holds x", out say) == BuildOutcome.Malformed,
              "a malformed release is refused, not attempted");
        Check(Builds.Decide(root, null, info, null, null, out say) == BuildOutcome.NotInstalled
              && Builds.Decide(root, local, info, null, null, out say) == BuildOutcome.NotInstalled,
              "an empty folder, or one with no game in it, offers a fresh install");

        // ...and the three that need a real install underneath them.
        string inst = PlantInstall(root, info, want);
        BuildInfo same = Builds.ReadInfo(SampleInfo("2026-09-20.aaaaaaa"));
        Check(Builds.Decide(inst, same, same, null, null, out say) == BuildOutcome.UpToDate
              && say.Contains("2026-09-20.aaaaaaa"),
              $"the installed build and the published one agreeing is the end of it ({say})");
        BuildDiff none = Builds.Compare(inst, want, new[] { "BUILD.sha256", Builds.InfoName, "NOTES.txt" });
        Check(none.Same && none.Wrong.Count == 0 && none.Missing.Count == 0,
              $"a matching install walks clean ({none.Wrong.Count} wrong, {none.Missing.Count} missing)");
        Check(Builds.Decide(inst, same, info, none, null, out say) == BuildOutcome.UpToDate,
              "different ids over identical files is up to date, not a download");

        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "Warships.pck"), "changed");
        System.IO.File.Delete(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "data_Warships_windows_x86_64", "Warships.dll"));
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "my_screenshot.png"), "mine");
        BuildDiff d = Builds.Compare(inst, want, new[] { "BUILD.sha256", Builds.InfoName, "NOTES.txt" });
        Check(!d.Same && d.Wrong.Count == 1 && d.Wrong[0].Path == "Warships.pck"
              && d.Missing.Count == 1 && d.Missing[0].Path.EndsWith("Warships.dll", StringComparison.Ordinal)
              && d.Extra.Contains("my_screenshot.png"),
              $"the walk names exactly what moved ({d.Wrong.Count} wrong, {d.Missing.Count} missing, {d.Extra.Count} unrecognised)");
        Check(Builds.Decide(inst, same, info, d, null, out say) == BuildOutcome.UpdateReady && say.Contains("2"),
              $"two changed files is an update, and it says how many ({say})");

        // ONLY THE PARTS THAT HOLD SOMETHING CHANGED. 3.3 MB fetched, 73 MB not: this is the whole
        // reason the build is hashed per file rather than replaced as one zip.
        BuildPlan plan = Builds.Plan(info, d);
        Check(plan.Parts.Count == 1 && plan.Parts[0].Id == "code" && plan.Files.Count == 2
              && plan.Bytes == 3355443,
              $"an ordinary release fetches one part, not both ({plan.Parts.Count} part, {plan.Bytes / 1048576.0:0.0} MB of 73.0)");

        // A FILE ON DISK THAT THE RELEASE DOES NOT NAME IS NEVER IN A WRITE SET.
        Check(!plan.Files.Any(e => e.Path == "my_screenshot.png")
              && System.IO.File.Exists(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "my_screenshot.png")),
              "a file the release never heard of is reported and left alone");

        // The game being open is asked before anything is downloaded, not after.
        string held = System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "held.bin");
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(held, "x");
        using (new System.IO.FileStream(held, System.IO.FileMode.Open, System.IO.FileAccess.Write, System.IO.FileShare.None))
            Check(Builds.Locked(held), "a file the game is holding open reads as locked");
        Check(!Builds.Locked(held) && !Builds.Locked(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "nothing.bin")),
              "a closed file, and a file that is not there, do not");
    }

    // A whole update, end to end, with no network and no launcher: a fake install, a fake release
    // in a folder, and the same code the launcher runs.
    void BuildApplyChecks()
    {
        string root = BuildScratch("apply");
        BuildInfo info = Builds.ReadInfo(SampleInfo("2026-09-23.ec0d138"));
        string rel = System.IO.Path.Combine(root, "release");
        string inst = System.IO.Path.Combine(root, "install");
        System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(rel);
        System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "data_Warships_windows_x86_64"));

        // The install: an old pck, an old dll, an exe that does not change, and a file of the
        // player's own sitting beside them.
        string pck = System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "Warships.pck");
        string dll = System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "data_Warships_windows_x86_64", "Warships.dll");
        string exe = System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "WarshipsGame.exe");
        string mine = System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "my_notes.txt");
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(pck, "OLD PCK");
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(dll, "OLD DLL");
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(exe, "ENGINE");
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(mine, "do not touch");

        // The release: the same exe, a new pck and a new dll, zipped into the part that holds them.
        string zip = System.IO.Path.Combine(rel, "code.zip");
        using (var z = System.IO.Compression.ZipFile.Open(zip, System.IO.Compression.ZipArchiveMode.Create))
        {
            using (var w = new System.IO.StreamWriter(z.CreateEntry("Warships.pck").Open())) w.Write("NEW PCK");
            using (var w = new System.IO.StreamWriter(z.CreateEntry("data_Warships_windows_x86_64/Warships.dll").Open())) w.Write("NEW DLL");
        }
        info.Parts.First(p => p.Id == "code").Sha = Builds.HashFile(zip);
        string manText = Builds.HashFile(exe) + "  WarshipsGame.exe\n"
                       + ShaOfText("NEW PCK") + "  Warships.pck\n"
                       + ShaOfText("NEW DLL") + "  data_Warships_windows_x86_64/Warships.dll\n";
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(rel, "BUILD.sha256"), manText);
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(rel, Builds.InfoName), SampleInfo("2026-09-23.ec0d138"));
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(rel, "NOTES.txt"), "what changed");

        var want = Builds.ReadManifest(manText);
        var src = new FolderBuildSource(rel);
        var d = Builds.Compare(inst, want, new[] { "BUILD.sha256", Builds.InfoName, "NOTES.txt" });
        var plan = Builds.Plan(info, d);
        Builds.Apply(inst, src, info, plan, null);

        Check(System.IO.File.ReadAllText(pck) == "NEW PCK" && System.IO.File.ReadAllText(dll) == "NEW DLL"
              && System.IO.File.ReadAllText(exe) == "ENGINE",
              "an update replaces what changed and leaves the 98 MB engine where it is");
        Check(System.IO.File.ReadAllText(mine) == "do not touch",
              "a file of the player's own beside the game is still there, unchanged");
        Check(System.IO.File.Exists(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, "BUILD.sha256"))
              && Builds.ReadInfo(System.IO.File.ReadAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, Builds.InfoName))).Build == "2026-09-23.ec0d138"
              && !System.IO.Directory.Exists(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, Builds.StageDir)),
              "the install now says which build it is, and nothing is left staged");
        Check(Builds.Compare(inst, want, new[] { "BUILD.sha256", Builds.InfoName, "NOTES.txt" }).Same,
              "and it walks clean against the release it just took");

        // A DOWNLOAD THAT DOES NOT MATCH NEVER REACHES THE INSTALL.
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(pck, "OLD PCK");
        var lying = Builds.ReadInfo(SampleInfo("2026-09-24.bbbbbbb"));
        var d2 = Builds.Compare(inst, want, new[] { "BUILD.sha256", Builds.InfoName, "NOTES.txt" });
        bool threw = false;
        try { Builds.Apply(inst, src, lying, Builds.Plan(lying, d2), null); }
        catch (System.IO.InvalidDataException) { threw = true; }
        Check(threw && System.IO.File.ReadAllText(pck) == "OLD PCK"
              && !System.IO.Directory.Exists(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, Builds.StageDir)),
              "a part whose checksum is wrong aborts, cleans up, and leaves the game that was there");

        // AN INTERRUPTED UPDATE FINISHES ITSELF. Staged, verified, journalled -- then stopped dead
        // before the swap, which is the one window where an install is half of each.
        string stage = System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, Builds.StageDir);
        string staged = System.IO.Path.Combine(stage, "files");
        System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(staged);
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(staged, "Warships.pck"), "NEW PCK");
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(stage, "JOURNAL"),
                                    "build=2026-09-23.ec0d138\npair=Warships.pck\n");
        Check(Builds.Resume(inst) && System.IO.File.ReadAllText(pck) == "NEW PCK"
              && !System.IO.Directory.Exists(stage),
              "an update stopped between the download and the swap finishes on the next start");
        Check(!Builds.Resume(inst), "and a start with nothing half-done has nothing to finish");
    }

    static string ShaOfText(string s)
    {
        using (var h = System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256.Create())
        {
            var b = h.ComputeHash(System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(s));
            var sb = new System.Text.StringBuilder(64);
            foreach (byte x in b) sb.Append(x.ToString("x2"));
            return sb.ToString();
        }
    }

    // A scratch folder under this run's own user:// -- which run.ps1 renames to WarshipsSmoke and
    // wipes each run, so none of this is ever near a real character file. NOT named OnDisk: that
    // helper already exists in this file and means something else.
    static string BuildScratch(string leaf)
    {
        string dir = System.IO.Path.Combine(ProjectSettings.GlobalizePath("user://"), "buildtest", leaf);
        if (System.IO.Directory.Exists(dir)) System.IO.Directory.Delete(dir, true);
        System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(dir);
        return dir;
    }

    // An install that matches a release exactly: every file the manifest names, with the content
    // whose hash the manifest claims. Written from the manifest so the check cannot disagree with
    // itself about what "matching" means.
    static string PlantInstall(string root, BuildInfo info, List<BuildEntry> want)
    {
        string inst = System.IO.Path.Combine(root, "planted");
        System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(inst);
        foreach (BuildEntry e in want)
        {
            string p = Builds.Resolve(inst, e.Path);
            System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory(System.IO.Path.GetDirectoryName(p));
            System.IO.File.WriteAllText(p, "");                      // empty: sha e3b0c4...
        }
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, info.Manifest),
                                    string.Join("\n", want.Select(e => Sha0 + "  " + e.Path)) + "\n");
        System.IO.File.WriteAllText(System.IO.Path.Combine(inst, Builds.InfoName), SampleInfo(info.Build));
        return inst;
    }

    void BossScaleChecks()
    {
        var row = Missions.ForLevel(1).Moves.First(m => m.Windup > 0 && m.Reach > 0);
        Check(Math.Abs(Missions.Quicken(1) - 1.0) < 1e-9
              && Math.Abs(Missions.Quicken(2) - 1.01) < 1e-9
              && Math.Abs(Missions.Quicken(11) - Math.Pow(1.01, 10)) < 1e-9
              && Math.Abs(Missions.Quicken(51) - Math.Pow(1.01, 50)) < 1e-9,
              $"a boss gains 1% a level on its wind-ups and its reach: x{Missions.Quicken(2):0.000} at level 2, x{Missions.Quicken(11):0.000} at 11, x{Missions.Quicken(51):0.000} at 51");

    }

    // ── THE RECYCLER: a hold turned back into salvage, and a lock so it cannot eat what you fly ──
    // A part could not be got rid of at all before this: a hold filled with commons a pilot would
    // never fit again, and salvage had nothing to buy but a refit and gear levels.
    async Task RecyclerChecks()
    {
        var yard = H.Yard;
        Character.GearHold.Clear(); Character.GearLocked.Clear();
        Character.Stow("bs_rapid_1"); Character.Stow("bs_rapid_1"); Character.Stow("cv_elite_3");
        yard.SetStock("salvage", 0);

        // A KIT PART IS NOT LOOT and is refused outright; a LOCKED part is refused too.
        Character.Stow("bs_main_battery");
        bool kitRefused = !yard.QueueScrap("bs_main_battery");
        Character.ToggleGearLock("cv_elite_3");
        bool lockedRefused = !yard.QueueScrap("cv_elite_3") && Character.GearLocked.Contains("cv_elite_3");

        // QUEUED: out of the hold at once, so it cannot be fitted or queued twice while it waits.
        bool queued = yard.QueueScrap("bs_rapid_1");
        bool goneFromHold = Character.GearHold.GetValueOrDefault("bs_rapid_1") == 1 && yard.ScrapPending == 1;
        // ...and TAKE BACK puts it straight back.
        bool back = yard.UnqueueScrap("bs_rapid_1") && Character.GearHold.GetValueOrDefault("bs_rapid_1") == 2 && yard.ScrapPending == 0;
        Check(kitRefused && lockedRefused && queued && goneFromHold && back,
              $"the recycler takes loot and nothing else: a hull's own mount refused, a locked part refused, a queued part out of the hold at once and back again when taken back ({yard.ScrapPending} queued)");

        // IT PAYS, one part every Economy.ScrapEvery, in salvage, by rarity.
        // ONE EPIC, because the pile will not hold still: the salvagers fill it and the hauler
        // takes loads off it while this runs, so the payment has to be big enough to read through
        // that. 600 against a fleet that moves tens either way in five seconds.
        Character.ToggleGearLock("cv_elite_3");                      // unlocked, to be scrapped
        bool epicQueued = yard.QueueScrap("cv_elite_3");
        double paid0 = yard.Stock("salvage");
        await Wait(Economy.ScrapEvery + 0.6);
        double paid = yard.Stock("salvage") - paid0;
        Check(epicQueued && paid > 450 && paid < 750 && yard.ScrapPending == 0
              && Math.Abs(Economy.ScrapValue(Rarity.Common) - 100) < 1e-6
              && Math.Abs(Economy.ScrapValue(Rarity.Rare) - 250) < 1e-6
              && Math.Abs(Economy.ScrapValue(Rarity.Epic) - 600) < 1e-6,
              $"it chews through the queue one part every {Economy.ScrapEvery:0} s and pays by rarity -- an epic is 600 ({paid:0} into a pile the fleet is also working), a rare 250, a common 100");
        Character.ToggleGearLock("cv_elite_3");                      // ...and locked again for the round trip below
        Character.Stow("cv_elite_3");

        // A LOCK IS THE PART ID'S, like its level, and it survives a round trip to disk.
        string keepId = Character.Id;
        Character.Id = "recycler"; Character.Save();
        Character.GearLocked.Clear();
        bool loaded = Character.Load("recycler") && Character.GearLocked.Contains("cv_elite_3");
        Character.Delete("recycler"); Character.Id = keepId;
        Check(loaded, $"a lock belongs to the part id and comes back off disk ({string.Join(",", Character.GearLocked)})");
        Character.GearHold.Clear(); Character.GearLocked.Clear();
    }

    // ── THE LANES: four courier runs to the outposts, a quarter of the passive income each ──
    // Everything asserted here is a literal from the owner's words: four lanes, 25% each, both
    // directions, a quarter off for one blockade and a half for two, and the gunship's own 42
    // coming back the other way. Where things STAND is varied (VaryNear); what they are worth is
    // not.
    async Task LaneChecks()
    {
        var Y = H.Yard;
        var lv = (System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<string, int>)typeof(Yard)
                 .GetField("_levels", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).GetValue(Y);
        var cdF = typeof(LaneGun).GetField("_cd", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance);
        double keepOre = Y.Stock("ore"), keepCredits = Y.Credits;
        var keepMe = Me.Position;
        // clear of every lane's stand by more than a raider's 2000 u notice, so nothing a check
        // puts on a lane comes after the pilot instead of holding it
        var park = VaryNear(Hub.BasePos + new Vector2(-700, 700), 150f);
        foreach (var r in H.Raiders.ToList()) r.TakeDamage(1e9);
        Me.Position = park; Me.Velocity = Vector2.Zero;
        await Wait(0.3);
        // 100 units delivered, and what the base is actually PAID for them. Yard.Deposit is the
        // one place the lanes are felt, and this is read in the SAME frame it is called, so the
        // fleet's own deliveries cannot move the figure.
        double Paid() { Y.SetStock("ore", 0); Y.Deposit("ore", 100); return Y.Stock("ore"); }

        // ── THE TABLE: four lanes, base to outpost, a quarter each ──────────────────────────
        Check(Lanes.All.Length == 4 && Lanes.All.All(l => Math.Abs(l.Share - 0.25) < 1e-9)
              && Math.Abs(Lanes.All.Sum(l => l.Share) - 1.0) < 1e-9
              && Enumerable.Range(0, Lanes.All.Length).All(i => Lanes.Ends(i).near == Hub.BasePos
                                                                && Lanes.Ends(i).far == Hub.Outposts[Lanes.All[i].Outpost].at)
              && Enumerable.Range(0, Lanes.All.Length).Select(Lanes.Name).SequenceEqual(new[] { "SE", "NE", "NW", "SW" }),
              $"four lanes, each from the base to one outpost, carrying a quarter of the passive income and a whole between them ({string.Join(", ", Enumerable.Range(0, Lanes.All.Length).Select(i => $"{Lanes.Name(i)} {Lanes.All[i].Share:0.00}"))})");

        // ── A COURIER RUNS BOTH WAYS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        var drones = Nodes<Courier>().ToList();
        var c0 = drones.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Lane == 0);
        var (nearEnd, farEnd) = Lanes.Run(0);
        double cyc = Lanes.Cycle(0);
        Check(c0 != null && drones.Count == Lanes.All.Sum(l => l.Drones) && drones.Count(c => c.Lane == 0) == 2
              && farEnd.DistanceTo(Hub.Outposts[0].at) < 200f && nearEnd.DistanceTo(Hub.BasePos) < 400f,
              $"every lane has its couriers, turning round beside the base and beside its outpost ({drones.Count} of {Lanes.All.Sum(l => l.Drones)} built)");
        c0.Phase = 0f;
        c0.Clock = 0;           await Wait(0.05); var atBase = c0.Position;      bool goingOut = c0.Outbound;
        c0.Clock = cyc * 0.25;  await Wait(0.05); var quarterOut = c0.Position;  bool stillOut = c0.Outbound;
        c0.Clock = cyc * 0.5;   await Wait(0.05); var atOutpost = c0.Position;
        c0.Clock = cyc * 0.75;  await Wait(0.05); var quarterBack = c0.Position; bool coming = !c0.Outbound;
        c0.Clock = cyc * 1.02;  await Wait(0.05); int runs = c0.Runs;
        double dBase = atBase.DistanceTo(Hub.BasePos), dOut = atOutpost.DistanceTo(Hub.BasePos);
        Check(goingOut && stillOut && coming && runs >= 2
              && atBase.DistanceTo(nearEnd) < 40f && atOutpost.DistanceTo(farEnd) < 40f
              && quarterOut.DistanceTo(Hub.BasePos) > dBase + 400f
              && quarterBack.DistanceTo(Hub.BasePos) < dOut - 400f,
              $"a courier runs BOTH WAYS on its lane -- out to the outpost, then home to the base, and round again ({dBase:0} u from the base -> {quarterOut.DistanceTo(Hub.BasePos):0} -> {dOut:0} -> {quarterBack.DistanceTo(Hub.BasePos):0}; {runs} one-way runs done)");

        // ── THE GUN AT THE FAR END ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        var guns = Nodes<LaneGun>().ToList();
        var gun = guns.FirstOrDefault(g => g.Lane == 0);
        Check(gun != null && guns.Count == Lanes.All.Length
              && gun.Position.DistanceTo(Hub.Outposts[0].at) < Hub.OutpostHeight
              && Nodes<Turret>(gun).Count() == 1
              && gun.Range > gun.Position.DistanceTo(Lanes.Stand(0)),
              $"every outpost carries a gun, on the one turret component, reaching the spot its own lane is cut on ({gun?.Range:0} u of the {gun?.Position.DistanceTo(Lanes.Stand(0)):0} u out to the stand)");
        // WHO IT MAY SHOOT is a filter, never a type test: raiding craft, and nothing of ours.
        var anyDummy = Nodes<TargetDummy>().FirstOrDefault();
        Check(!Targeting.Craft.Allows(Me) && !Targeting.Craft.Allows(Y.Hauler) && !Targeting.Craft.Allows(Y.Gatherers[0])
              && (H.Deployed.Count == 0 || !Targeting.Craft.Allows(H.Deployed[0]))
              && (anyDummy == null || !Targeting.Craft.Allows(anyDummy)),
              "the filter keeps the outposts off their own side: a pilot, the hauler, a miner, a dropped turret and a practice dummy are none of them raiding craft");
        Check(Math.Abs(gun.Range - 1200) < 1e-3 && Math.Abs(gun.Interval - 10.0) < 1e-9 && Math.Abs(gun.Speed - 300) < 1e-3,
              $"an unbought outpost gun: 1200 u, one missile every 10 s (6 a minute), 300 u/s ({gun.Range:0} u, {gun.Interval:0.00} s, {gun.Speed:0} u/s)");
        Y.Credits = 100000;
        bool three = Y.TryBuy(Lanes.RangeId) && Y.TryBuy(Lanes.RateId) && Y.TryBuy(Lanes.SpeedId);
        Check(three && Economy.All.Count(u => u.Tab == "OUTPOSTS") == 3 && Economy.Tabs.Contains("OUTPOSTS")
              && Math.Abs(gun.Range - 1320) < 1e-3 && Math.Abs(gun.Interval - 9.0909) < 1e-3 && Math.Abs(gun.Speed - 330) < 1e-3,
              $"the OUTPOSTS tab buys range, rate of fire and missile speed, +10% a level, for every outpost at once: {gun.Range:0} u, {gun.Interval:0.000} s a missile, {gun.Speed:0} u/s");
        lv.Remove(Lanes.RangeId); lv.Remove(Lanes.RateId); lv.Remove(Lanes.SpeedId);

        // NOTHING OF OURS DRAWS A SHOT: the pilot parked on the very spot a blockade stands on.
        Me.Position = Lanes.Stand(0); Me.Velocity = Vector2.Zero;
        int blasts0 = H.BlastsPending, flying0 = Nodes<MissileVisual>().Count();
        await Wait(3.0);
        Check(H.BlastsPending <= blasts0 && Nodes<MissileVisual>().Count() <= flying0 && gun.Aimed == null,
              $"and it throws nothing at its own side: a pilot sitting on the stand for 3 s, well inside its 1200 u, is never even aimed at ({H.BlastsPending - blasts0} thrown)");
        Me.Position = park; Me.Velocity = Vector2.Zero;
        await Wait(0.3);

        // ── A CUT LANE STOPS PAYING: A QUARTER FOR ONE, A HALF FOR TWO ──────────────────────
        double whole = Paid();
        var cutA = H.SpawnRaider(VaryNear(Lanes.Stand(0), 200f), Enemies.Webifier);
        await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        cutA.Hp = 5000;                                  // it is the thing being blockaded WITH
        double oneCut = Paid();
        bool threeQuarters = Math.Abs(Lanes.Flow(H) - 0.75) < 1e-9;
        var heldAt = c0.Position; double heldClock = c0.Clock;
        var cutB = H.SpawnRaider(VaryNear(Lanes.Stand(1), 200f), Enemies.Webifier);
        await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        cutB.Hp = 5000;
        double twoCut = Paid();
        Check(Math.Abs(whole - 100) < 1e-9 && Math.Abs(oneCut - 75) < 1e-9 && Math.Abs(twoCut - 50) < 1e-9
              && threeQuarters && Math.Abs(Lanes.Flow(H) - 0.5) < 1e-9
              && Lanes.Cut(H, 0) && Lanes.Cut(H, 1) && !Lanes.Cut(H, 2) && !Lanes.Cut(H, 3),
              $"one lane blockaded costs exactly a quarter of the passive income and two lanes a half: 100 units delivered pay {whole:0}, then {oneCut:0}, then {twoCut:0}");
        // ...and the courier on a cut lane holds where it is: the flow has stopped, visibly
        await Wait(0.6);
        Check(c0.Held && c0.Position.DistanceTo(heldAt) < 1f && Math.Abs(c0.Clock - heldClock) < 1e-6,
              $"the cut lane's couriers hold where they are, carrying nothing ({c0.Position.DistanceTo(heldAt):0.0} u in 0.6 s)");

        // ── THE OUTPOST ANSWERS: the heavy fighter's own missile, friendly-coloured ─────────
        cutB.TakeDamage(1e9);                            // one blockader, so one gun is firing
        await Wait(0.5);
        // held on the spot for a few frames first, so the LEAD is zero and this check is about the
        // blast: the prediction itself is proved against literals where Missiles.Predict is.
        var markAt = cutA.Position;
        for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) { cutA.Position = markAt; await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame); }
        cdF.SetValue(gun, 0.0);                          // its reload may be part-spent on the escort's hunters
        double hp0 = cutA.Hp;
        FxNode mark = null; MissileVisual flying = null;
        for (int i = 0; i < 60 * 3 && flying == null; i++)
        {
            cutA.Position = markAt;
            await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
            // THIS gun's, at THIS blockader: an outpost missile aimed where the blockader stands
            flying = Nodes<MissileVisual>().FirstOrDefault(mv => mv.Side == Missiles.Outpost && mv.To.DistanceTo(markAt) < 25f);
            mark = Nodes<FxNode>().FirstOrDefault(fn => fn.Id == Fx.AimZone && Math.Abs(fn.Radius - 90f) < 0.1f
                                                       && fn.Position.DistanceTo(markAt) < 25f);
        }
        bool marked = flying != null && mark != null && mark.Warn && mark.Anchor == Fx.World
                      && ReferenceEquals(gun.Aimed, cutA);
        for (int i = 0; i < 60 * 6 && cutA.Hp >= hp0; i++)
        { cutA.Position = markAt; await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame); }
        Check(marked && Math.Abs(hp0 - cutA.Hp - 42) < 1e-6,
              $"the outpost throws the heavy fighter's own predicted missile at the blockader, marks where it will land in friendly colours, and lands the gunship's 42 there ({hp0 - cutA.Hp:0} off the blockader)");

        // ── A BLOCKADE IS A ROW OF Waves.All, holding the lane's own stand ─────────────────
        var plainRow = Waves.For(WaveTrigger.Blockade, new WaveBrief { Index = 0 });
        var lateRow = Waves.For(WaveTrigger.Blockade, new WaveBrief { Index = 2 });
        H.Blockade(0);
        await Wait(0.3);
        var squad = H.Raiders.Where(r => r != cutA).ToList();
        Check(plainRow != null && plainRow.Id == "blockade" && Math.Abs(plainRow.Hold - 200f) < 1e-3 && plainRow.Crew.Length == 2
              && lateRow != null && lateRow.Id == "blockade_heavy" && lateRow.Crew.Length == 3
              && squad.Count == 4 && squad.Count(r => r.Heavy) == 1
              && squad.All(r => r.Position.DistanceTo(Lanes.Stand(0)) <= Lanes.Hold)
              && squad.All(r => r.Station.DistanceTo(Lanes.Stand(0)) < 1f && Math.Abs(r.Circuit - 200f) < 1e-3)
              && Lanes.Cut(H, 0) && Math.Abs(Lanes.Flow(H) - 0.75) < 1e-9,
              $"a blockade is a trigger and a row, not a spawner: three lights and a heavy holding a 200 u ring on the lane's own stand, and the base paid three quarters ({squad.Count} sent, {Lanes.Flow(H) * 100:0}% flow)");

        // ── CLEARING IT RESTORES THE INCOME ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        foreach (var r in H.Raiders.ToList()) r.TakeDamage(1e9);
        await Wait(0.3);
        double again = Paid();
        Check(Enumerable.Range(0, Lanes.All.Length).All(i => !Lanes.Cut(H, i))
              && Math.Abs(Lanes.Flow(H) - 1.0) < 1e-9 && Math.Abs(again - 100) < 1e-9
              && Lanes.Readout(H).Length == 0,
              $"clearing the blockade restores the income at once: 100 units delivered pay {again:0} again, and the HUD stops reporting a cut lane");

        Y.SetStock("ore", keepOre); Y.Credits = keepCredits;
        Me.Position = keepMe; Me.Velocity = Vector2.Zero;
        await Wait(0.2);
    }

    void GearLevelChecks()
    {
        var battery = Equipment.ById("bs_rapid_1");                  // faster guns, lighter shells
        if (battery == null) { Check(false, "gear levels: no bs_rapid_1 to level"); return; }

        double first = Equipment.NextLevelCost(battery.Id);
        Character.GearLevel[battery.Id] = 1;  double second = Equipment.NextLevelCost(battery.Id);
        Character.GearLevel[battery.Id] = 2;  double third  = Equipment.NextLevelCost(battery.Id);
        Character.GearLevel[battery.Id] = Equipment.MaxLevel;
        double ceiling = Equipment.NextLevelCost(battery.Id);
        double whole = 0; for (int k = 0; k < Equipment.MaxLevel; k++) whole += Math.Round(100 * Math.Pow(1.25, k));
        Check(Math.Abs(first - 100) < 1e-6 && Math.Abs(second - 125) < 1e-6 && Math.Abs(third - 156) < 1e-6
              && ceiling < 0 && Equipment.MaxLevel * Equipment.LevelStep == 2.0 && Math.Abs(whole - 3008864) < 2,
              $"a level costs 100 salvage and a quarter more each time, stopping at +200%: {first:0}, {second:0}, {third:0}, and {whole:0} for the whole ladder of {Equipment.MaxLevel}");

        // WHAT IT LIFTS: the part's own stats, and not what it takes in exchange.
        Character.GearLevel.Clear();
        var worn = Equipment.Default(ShipClass.Battleship);
        worn[Array.IndexOf(Equipment.Core, battery.Slot)] = battery.Id;
        var bare = Equipment.Bonuses(ShipClass.Battleship, worn);
        Character.GearLevel[battery.Id] = 10;                        // +50%
        var lifted = Equipment.Bonuses(ShipClass.Battleship, worn);
        string up = battery.Ups.FirstOrDefault(), down = battery.Pct.Keys.FirstOrDefault(k => Array.IndexOf(battery.Ups, k) < 0);
        Check(up != null && down != null
              && Math.Abs(lifted[up] - bare[up] * 1.5) < 1e-9 && Math.Abs(lifted[down] - bare[down]) < 1e-9,
              $"ten levels lift what the part is FOR by half and leave what it costs alone: {up} {bare[up] * 100:0.#}% -> {lifted[up] * 100:0.#}%, {down} {bare[down] * 100:0.#}% either way");

        // A LEVEL IS THE ID'S, and it survives a round trip to disk. Under a scratch id of its own:
        // the pilot this run is flying has a base saved against it.
        string keepId = Character.Id;
        Character.Id = "gearlevel"; Character.Save();
        Character.GearLevel.Clear();
        bool loaded = Character.Load("gearlevel") && Equipment.LevelOf(battery.Id) == 10;
        Check(loaded && Equipment.LevelOf("bs_rapid_2") == 0,
              $"a level belongs to the part id, and comes back off disk ({Equipment.LevelOf(battery.Id)} on the battery, {Equipment.LevelOf("bs_rapid_2")} on the mark II)");
        Character.Delete("gearlevel");
        Character.GearLevel.Clear(); Character.Id = keepId;
    }

    // A wider view than before: a boss's reach grows with the level, and a fight whose edges are
    // off screen is a fight fought on the minimap.
    void ZoomChecks()
    {
        H.SetZoom(0.0001f);                                   // as far out as the wheel will go
        float out0 = H.ZoomLevel;
        H.SetZoom(1000f);                                     // ...and as far in
        float in0 = H.ZoomLevel;
        H.SetZoom(Hub.DefaultZoom);
        Check(Math.Abs(out0 - Hub.DefaultZoom / 1.53f) < 1e-6 && Math.Abs(in0 - Hub.DefaultZoom * 1.5f) < 1e-6
              && Math.Abs(Hub.ZoomOutMax / 1.33f - 1.15f) < 0.005f,
              $"the wheel reaches 15% further out than it did -- 1.33 of the default was the limit, 1.53 is ({out0:0.000} out, {in0:0.000} in)");
    }

    // ── THE SKY: layered, and every layer moving at its own speed ───────────────────────────────
    // What this replaces could not move AT ALL: one TextureRect anchored FullRect to the screen,
    // so a ship at 190 u/s crossed a starfield that never shifted a pixel. The rows are proved
    // against literals here; that they actually MOVE, and move by DIFFERENT amounts, is proved by
    // shifting the camera and reading them back -- which is the only check that would have caught
    // the thing being fixed.
    async Task SkyChecks()
    {
        var sky = H.GetNodeOrNull<CanvasLayer>("Stars");
        var layers = sky == null ? new List<Parallax2D>() : Nodes<Parallax2D>(sky).ToList();
        Check(sky != null && sky.Layer == -100 && layers.Count == Sky.All.Length && Sky.All.Length == 3
              && layers.Select(l => l.Name.ToString()).SequenceEqual(Sky.All.Select(r => "Sky_" + r.Id)),
              $"the sky is a layer per row, all of it behind the world ({layers.Count} of {Sky.All.Length} rows on layer {sky?.Layer})");

        // FAR TO NEAR, strictly. The illusion IS the ordering: equal drifts are one flat sheet,
        // and a row out of order reads as the distance running backwards. Every row must drift
        // MORE than nothing -- a 0 is the static sky this replaced -- and less than 0.6, past
        // which the stars stop reading as distance and start reading as debris going by.
        bool climbs = true;
        for (int i = 1; i < Sky.All.Length; i++) if (Sky.All[i].Drift <= Sky.All[i - 1].Drift) climbs = false;
        Check(climbs && Sky.All.All(r => r.Drift > 0f && r.Drift < 0.6f)
              && Math.Abs(Sky.All[0].Drift - 0.08f) < 1e-6 && Math.Abs(Sky.All[Sky.All.Length - 1].Drift - 0.45f) < 1e-6,
              $"every layer moves and none keeps up: {string.Join(" < ", Sky.All.Select(r => r.Drift.ToString("0.00")))} of the world's motion, ordered far to near");

        // A ROW'S SCALE REACHES ITS REPEAT. RepeatSize is the tile's DRAWN size, so a row whose
        // scale is not in it seams mid-tile and the whole field visibly steps as it crosses.
        bool tiles = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < layers.Count; i++)
        {
            var row = Sky.All[i];
            var art = Nodes<Sprite2D>(layers[i]).FirstOrDefault();
            if (art?.Texture == null) { tiles = false; break; }
            if (Math.Abs(layers[i].RepeatSize.X - art.Texture.GetWidth() * row.Scale) > 0.5f) tiles = false;
            // ...and the row's Drift reaches the engine as its INVERSE, which is the one place
            // the two senses meet and the one place a future row can be silently reversed.
            if (Math.Abs(layers[i].ScrollScale.X - (1f - row.Drift)) > 1e-6) tiles = false;
            if (Math.Abs(art.Scale.X - row.Scale) > 1e-6) tiles = false;
        }
        Check(tiles && layers.Count > 0,
              $"each layer repeats at its own drawn size and scrolls at its own row's rate ({layers.Count} layers)");

        // AND IT MOVES. The camera goes a long way sideways; every layer must shift, and a NEARER
        // one must shift further than the one behind it. This is the check the old sky failed.
        // MEASURED WHERE IT IS DRAWN. Parallax2D.ScreenOffset is the RAW camera offset and reads
        // the same on every layer -- measuring it said all three moved 4000 u and proved nothing.
        // The transform-with-canvas is where the art actually lands on the screen.
        var art0 = layers.Select(l => Nodes<Sprite2D>(l).FirstOrDefault()).ToList();
        // ...AND MEASURED OVER A SHORT HOP. A layer REPEATS, so its origin jumps by whole tiles as
        // it re-tiles: the smallest tile here is 563 u (1024 px of stars.png at the far row's
        // 0.55), and a 4000 u move wrapped every layer several times, which read as 4243 / 4144 /
        // 4350 -- noise around the raw distance, telling us nothing. 200 u wraps nothing.
        var wasAt = Me.Position;
        var before = art0.Select(a2 => a2 == null ? 0f : a2.GetGlobalTransformWithCanvas().Origin.X).ToList();
        Me.Position = wasAt + new Vector2(200, 0);
        for (int f = 0; f < 6; f++) await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        var moved = art0.Select((a2, i) => a2 == null ? 0f : Math.Abs(a2.GetGlobalTransformWithCanvas().Origin.X - before[i])).ToList();
        bool anyMoved = moved.Any(d => d > 1f);
        bool deeper = true;
        for (int i = 1; i < moved.Count; i++) if (moved[i] <= moved[i - 1]) deeper = false;
        // ...AND BY THE SHARE ITS ROW ASKED FOR. Each layer's travel over the same hop, divided by
        // its own Drift, must come to the same camera distance -- which is what makes this a check
        // on the NUMBERS in the table and not merely on the ordering of them.
        bool byShare = true;
        double unit = moved.Count > 0 ? moved[0] / Sky.All[0].Drift : 0;
        for (int i = 1; i < moved.Count; i++)
            if (Math.Abs(moved[i] / Sky.All[i].Drift - unit) > unit * 0.05) byShare = false;
        Me.Position = wasAt;
        await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        Check(anyMoved && deeper && byShare,
              $"200 u of ship moves every layer on screen, each nearer one further than the one behind it, and each by its own row's share ({string.Join(", ", moved.Select(d => d.ToString("0.0")))} u over {string.Join(", ", Sky.All.Select(r => r.Drift.ToString("0.00")))})");
    }

    // ── THE SOFT TUTORIAL: a card at a time, CONTINUE, and SKIP in the top right ────────────────
    // On a FIRST character only. It is an order of hint ids rather than a second copy of the
    // words, so a card here and a card met in play are the same card, and a card dismissed here is
    // never shown again.
    async Task TourChecks()
    {
        var tour = Nodes<Tour>().FirstOrDefault();
        Check(tour != null && Hints.Tour.Length >= 6 && Hints.Tour.All(id => Hints.All.ContainsKey(id))
              && Hints.Tour.Distinct().Count() == Hints.Tour.Length,
              $"the tour is an ORDER of hints, not a second copy of them: {Hints.Tour.Length} steps, every one a card the game already has, none of them twice");
        if (tour == null) return;

        // A pilot that has met anything is not new, and is never offered it.
        bool offeredToVeteran = false;
        var was = new System.Collections.Generic.HashSet<string>(Character.HintsSeen);
        Character.HintsSeen.Add("flight");
        var late = new Tour { Hub = H }; AddChild(late); late.StartIfNew();
        offeredToVeteran = late.Running;
        late.QueueFree();
        Character.HintsSeen.Clear(); foreach (var id in was) Character.HintsSeen.Add(id);
        Check(!offeredToVeteran, "a pilot that has met anything at all is not walked through it");

        // CONTINUE steps forward and marks the card seen; the last one reads FLY.
        Character.HintsSeen.Clear(); Character.TourDone = false;
        var fresh = new Tour { Hub = H }; AddChild(fresh); fresh.StartIfNew();
        bool started = fresh.Running;
        var cont = Nodes<Button>(fresh).First(b => b.Name == "Continue");
        var skipBtn = Nodes<Button>(fresh).First(b => b.Name == "Skip");
        cont.EmitSignal(BaseButton.SignalName.Pressed);
        await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        bool stepped = Character.HintsSeen.Contains(Hints.Tour[0]) && fresh.Running;
        // SKIP ends it and marks the WHOLE tour seen, so the same pilot is not asked again.
        skipBtn.EmitSignal(BaseButton.SignalName.Pressed);
        await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
        bool skipped = Hints.Tour.All(Character.HintsSeen.Contains) && Character.TourDone;
        Check(started && stepped && skipped,
              $"CONTINUE marks a card seen and moves on; SKIP ends it and marks every card on it, so nothing is ever said twice ({Character.HintsSeen.Count} seen, done {Character.TourDone})");
        Character.HintsSeen.Clear(); Character.TourDone = false;
        foreach (var id in was) Character.HintsSeen.Add(id);
    }

    void RefitChecks()
    {
        Character.NewBlank();
        Character.Level = 40; Character.Points = 39; Character.Exp = 560;     // 560 of 1000 toward 41
        bool bought = Progression.TryBuy("hull") && Progression.TryBuy("hull") && Progression.TryBuy("turn");
        int pointsBefore = Character.Points, hullBefore = Character.Bought[1], turnBefore = Character.Bought[0];
        var (undone, back) = Progression.Refit();
        Check(bought && undone == "Rudder" && back == 1 && Character.Bought[0] == turnBefore - 1
              && Character.Bought[1] == hullBefore && Character.Level == 39 && Character.Exp == 560
              && Character.Points == pointsBefore + 1 - 1,
              $"a refit takes a level and undoes the LAST point bought -- rudder, not the two hull levels that cost more -- refunds what it cost, and leaves the progress toward the next level alone ({undone} came off for {back} back, level {Character.Level}, {Character.Exp} of 1000, {Character.Points} points)");

        // ...and a pilot from before the order was written down loses its DEAREST point instead,
        // which is the most a file with nothing to read can honestly say.
        Character.NewBlank();
        Character.Level = 40; Character.Points = 39;
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) Progression.TryBuy("hull");
        Progression.TryBuy("speed");
        Character.Spent.Clear();                                              // as an old file loads: no order at all
        var (old, oldBack) = Progression.Refit();
        Check(old == "Hull" && oldBack == 4 && Character.Bought[1] == 3,
              $"a pilot saved before the order was recorded loses its dearest point instead: the fourth hull level, {oldBack} points back ({old})");
        Character.NewBlank();
    }

    async Task Solo()
    {
        Check(H != null, "hub loaded");
        Check(Count<PlayerShip>() == 1 && Me != null, "one ship named Ship_1");
        Check(Count<CharacterCreator>() == 0, "no creator on entry");

        // ── THE TUTORIAL: a new pilot's first hub entry shows FLYING in the corner; THE BASE waits ──
        {
            var hn = H.Hints;
            var card = Nodes<PanelContainer>(hn).FirstOrDefault(p => p.Name == "HintCard");
            Label CardTitle() => Nodes<Label>(card).First();
            Check(card != null && card.Visible && CardTitle().Text == "FLYING" && Character.HintsSeen.Contains("flight") && HintQueue.Contains("base"),
                  $"a new pilot's first hub entry: FLYING in the corner, THE BASE waiting its turn ({CardTitle()?.Text}; queue {string.Join(",", HintQueue)})");
            var ctrls = Nodes<Control>(hn).ToList();
            Check(ctrls.Count >= 4 && ctrls.All(c => c.MouseFilter == Control.MouseFilterEnum.Ignore && c.FocusMode == Control.FocusModeEnum.None),
                  $"the hint card never takes input: every part of it lets clicks through and never holds the keyboard ({ctrls.Count} controls)");
            // the Esc menu covers the game: the card's clock holds
            var ageF = typeof(Hints).GetField("_age", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance);
            H.ToggleEscMenu(); await Wait(0.1);
            double age0 = (double)ageF.GetValue(hn); await Wait(2.0); double age1 = (double)ageF.GetValue(hn);
            H.ToggleEscMenu(); await Wait(1.0); double age2 = (double)ageF.GetValue(hn);
            Check(Math.Abs(age1 - age0) < 1e-9 && Math.Abs(age2 - age1 - 1.0) < 0.05, $"the card's clock holds while the Esc menu is open ({age0:0.00} -> {age1:0.00} in 2 s; +{age2 - age1:0.00} in 1 s after)");
            // ...and under the ship menu, and the pilot's stats (K)
            Priv(H, "OpenCreator"); await Wait(0.1);
            double ageC0 = (double)ageF.GetValue(hn); await Wait(0.5); double ageC1 = (double)ageF.GetValue(hn);
            bool creatorUp = H.CreatorOpen;
            Key(global::Godot.Key.Escape); await Wait(0.1);
            Key(global::Godot.Key.K); await Wait(0.1);
            double ageK0 = (double)ageF.GetValue(hn); await Wait(0.5); double ageK1 = (double)ageF.GetValue(hn);
            bool statsUp = H.StatsOpen;
            Key(global::Godot.Key.K); await Wait(0.1);
            Check(creatorUp && statsUp && !H.CreatorOpen && !H.StatsOpen && Math.Abs(ageC1 - ageC0) < 1e-9 && Math.Abs(ageK1 - ageK0) < 1e-9,
                  $"...and under the ship menu and the pilot's stats (K) ({ageC0:0.00} -> {ageC1:0.00}; {ageK0:0.00} -> {ageK1:0.00})");
            // 8 s in full, a 1 s fade, then the next
            double fadeAt = -1, halfAlpha = -1;
            for (int i = 0; i < 60 * 12 && CardTitle().Text == "FLYING"; i++)
            {
                double age = (double)ageF.GetValue(hn);
                if (fadeAt < 0 && card.Modulate.A < 1f) fadeAt = age;
                if (halfAlpha < 0 && age >= 8.5) halfAlpha = card.Modulate.A;
                await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
            }
            Check(Math.Abs(fadeAt - 8.0) < 0.05 && Math.Abs(halfAlpha - 0.5) < 0.1 && CardTitle().Text == "THE BASE" && card.Visible,
                  $"a card stays 8 s in full, fades over 1 s, and the next takes its place (fading at {fadeAt:0.00} s, half gone at 8.5 s: {halfAlpha:0.00})");
            // several at once queue in order; one already waiting is not queued twice
            H.Hints.Meet("tio"); H.Hints.Meet("raid"); H.Hints.Meet("tio");
            Check(CardTitle().Text == "THE BASE" && HintQueue.SequenceEqual(new[] { "tio", "raid" }),
                  $"hints met at once wait their turn, in order, each once ({string.Join(",", HintQueue)})");
            // remembered per character: on its file within 3 s -- and never shown again
            typeof(Yard).GetField("_saveCd", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).SetValue(H.Yard, 999.0);
            await Wait(0.4); bool early = ((string)OnDisk("hints", "seen", "")).Split(',').Contains("base");
            await Wait(2.6); bool late = ((string)OnDisk("hints", "seen", "")).Split(',').Contains("base");
            H.Hints.Meet("flight");                               // shown, and long finished
            Check(!early && late && !HintQueue.Contains("flight") && HintShowing != "flight",
                  $"a hint shown is on the pilot's file within 3 s, and never shown again (at 0.4 s {early}, at 3.0 s {late}; queue {string.Join(",", HintQueue)})");
            typeof(Yard).GetField("_saveCd", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).SetValue(H.Yard, 30.0);
            // the triggers: each system the first time a pilot meets it
            var me = Me; var hd1 = H.GetNode<TargetDummy>("TargetDummy1"); var here = me.Position;
            Unmeet("target", "abilities", "tio", "warp", "stasis", "base");
            // west of dummy 1: every other target is more than 700 u from here
            me.Position = hd1.Position + new Vector2(-520, 0); me.Velocity = Vector2.Zero; await Wait(0.1);
            bool farT = Met("target");
            me.Position = hd1.Position + new Vector2(-480, 0); await Wait(0.1);
            Check(!farT && Met("target"), "TARGETING: met within 500 u of something to target, not at 520");
            bool noSel = Met("abilities");
            H.SelectTarget(hd1); await Wait(0.1);
            Check(!noSel && Met("abilities"), "ABILITIES: met with the first target selected");
            H.ClearSelection();
            me.Position = Hub.BasePos + new Vector2(610, 0); await Wait(0.1);
            bool farBase = Met("base");
            me.Position = Hub.BasePos + new Vector2(590, 0); await Wait(0.1);
            Check(!farBase && Met("base"), "THE BASE: met within 600 u of it, not at 610");
            me.Position = Hub.TioPos + new Vector2(450, 0); await Wait(0.1);
            bool farTio = Met("tio");
            me.Position = Hub.TioPos + new Vector2(350, 0); await Wait(0.1);
            bool nearTio = Met("tio");
            Unmeet("tio"); me.Position = Hub.TioPos + new Vector2(700, 0); await Wait(0.1);
            H.OpenTio(); await Wait(0.1); bool byOpen = Met("tio"); Key(global::Godot.Key.Escape); await Wait(0.1);
            Check(!farTio && nearTio && byOpen, $"THE TIO: met within 400 u of it, not at 450 -- or on opening it from anywhere ({farTio}, {nearTio}, {byOpen})");
            me.Position = here;
            H.SelectWaypoint("NEAR", here + new Vector2(0, 1450), 200f); await Wait(0.1);
            bool nearWp = Met("warp");
            H.SelectWaypoint("FAR", here + new Vector2(0, 1550), 200f); await Wait(0.1);
            Check(!nearWp && Met("warp"), "WARP: met with a target or waypoint more than 1500 u away: not at 1450, at 1550");
            H.ClearSelection();
            me.TakeDamage(me.Hp + 1); await Wait(0.2);
            Check(Met("stasis"), "STASIS: met when the ship is shot down");
            typeof(PlayerShip).GetField("_stasis", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).SetValue(me, 0.0);
            me.UseAbility("reboard", 0); await Wait(0.1); me.Hp = me.MaxHp; me.Position = here; me.Velocity = Vector2.Zero;
            // THE OFF SWITCH, in the Esc menu: the pilot's, saved at once; the card goes with it
            H.ToggleEscMenu(); await Wait(0.1);
            var sw = Nodes<Button>().FirstOrDefault(b => b.Name == "HintsToggle");
            bool onByDefault = sw != null && sw.Text == "HINTS: ON";
            sw?.EmitSignal(BaseButton.SignalName.Pressed); await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
            bool offSaved = Character.HintsOff && (bool)OnDisk("hints", "off", false) && sw.Text == "HINTS: OFF";
            await ToSignal(GetTree(), SceneTree.SignalName.ProcessFrame);
            H.Hints.Meet("loot");
            bool gone = !card.Visible && HintQueue.Count == 0 && !Met("loot");
            sw?.EmitSignal(BaseButton.SignalName.Pressed); await Wait(0.05);
            Check(onByDefault && offSaved && gone && !Character.HintsOff && !(bool)OnDisk("hints", "off", true) && sw.Text == "HINTS: ON",
                  $"the Esc menu turns hints off -- for this pilot, saved at once -- and the card and its queue go with them ({onByDefault}, {offSaved}, {gone})");
            H.ToggleEscMenu(); await Wait(0.1);
        }

        // the ship menu is behind REFIT in the BASE menu now, and it costs 10%
        Key(global::Godot.Key.C); await Wait(0.1);
        Check(Count<CharacterCreator>() == 0, "C no longer opens the ship menu");
        H.Yard.SetStock("ore", 1000); H.Yard.SetStock("salvage", 500); H.Yard.Credits = 200;
        Key(global::Godot.Key.B); await Wait(0.1);
        var bp = Nodes<BasePanel>().FirstOrDefault();
        Check(bp != null, "B opens the base menu");
        // THE THEME HAS TO ACTUALLY REACH THE BUTTONS, and for the project's whole history it did
        // not: a theme set on the root window does not cross a CanvasLayer, every piece of UI here
        // hangs off one, and so every button in the game drew Godot's stock theme. It went unnoticed
        // because the stock theme is ALSO a dark rounded rectangle -- it took a deliberately red
        // stylebox and a pixel count to expose it. Compared with the palette as literals rather than
        // with Ui.Card, so this fails both when a subtree stops inheriting and when the look changes
        // by accident. Counting the buttons first: an empty list must not pass as "all themed".
        var btns = Nodes<Button>().ToList();
        var unthemed = btns.Where(b => (b.GetThemeStylebox("normal") as StyleBoxFlat) is not StyleBoxFlat sb
                                       || sb.BgColor != new Color(0.102f, 0.129f, 0.173f)
                                       || sb.BorderColor != new Color(0.184f, 0.227f, 0.302f)).ToList();
        Check(btns.Count >= 8 && unthemed.Count == 0,
              $"all {btns.Count} buttons take the game's theme, not Godot's" +
              (unthemed.Count > 0 ? $" -- {unthemed.Count} do not: {string.Join(", ", unthemed.Take(5).Select(b => b.GetParent()?.Name + "/" + b.Name))}" : ""));
        ShowTab(bp, "REFIT");
        var reset = Nodes<Button>(bp).First(b => b.Name == "Reset");
        // The docked hauler keeps loading from stock every frame, so amounts are read
